lines.en: Somewhere in the urban district, beneath a shining star...
: Hey, sorry I’m late. I ran into an issue with a pair of handcuffs.
: No worries. Any time your punctuality takes a hit I kind of just assume it’s due to some BDSM-related mishap. Also, I invited Karin. Hope that’s cool.

: Heeeey. That’s me. I’m the other girl from the swimsuit contest thing who also felt like it should have been canceled but wasn’t able to speak up because I want my sister to like me. Nice to meet you.
: Nice to meet you as well. Now go home. My quota for human contact today caps out at one person and Imani already counts as at least four.
: Yo, chill. Karin isn’t going anywhere. She still needs a Halloween costume too and she’s part of the “I know Imani is a monster underneath her clothes” club.
: I actually like your scars. They add personality. But I suppose that is a double-edged sword as you already have too much of that to begin with.
: You could have just introduced me as a member of the swim club too...that would have worked.
: Yeah, maybe in the context of a situation where I’d be keeping my clothes on. But it’s not like I can just throw a hat on and go to this year’s party as “Hat Imani.”
: I think Hat Imani sounds cute. It’s like normal Imani just...there’s a hat. And it’s...
: The hat is on her.
: Is this what you wanted? If we needed someone awkward, we could have just invited Rika. At least she’s of age.
: I’m sorry. I’ll try to be better.
: Damn it, Wakana. Now look what you’ve done. You’ve made the only wholesome girl in all of Kumon-mi sad. And if you wind up being the one to lead her down a dark path, I won’t ever forgive you.
: Forgiveness be damned. I will not follow in the footsteps of you and Arakawa by spending what little free time I have with students. I have better things to do.
: Bro, we’re just buying costumes. It’s not like we’re inviting her out to the bar.
: But hey, even if we were, she’d probably just bail on me last minute anyway since that is apparently what you guys do now.
: Yeah, I’m looking at you.
: I had nothing to do with that. It was Rika’s idea.
: Mmmmmhm. Well, thanks. I’m sure it went down exactly how she wanted it to.
: Was there...some sort of issue recently? Is it something I’m allowed to know?
: Hah. There’s a guy I like, but the guy doesn’t like me. Or...does like me, but also likes someone else.
: So he doesn’t want to like me any harder than he currently likes me because it might make us like each other less. Even though I currently want him to like me so hard that it shatters my pelvis.
: Adult relationships sound complicated. I didn’t even know that you could like someone with...that amount of force.
: Because, again, you are the only wholesome girl in this entire city. So make sure you don’t listen to anything Wakana says as her world view may accidentally gothify you.
: Everything I do is for the greater good. Which is why the first place on our list today is one of my favorite shops.
: If I am going to gothify anyone I would prefer it happens early before my medication begins to wear off.
: Good. The sooner I can get away from these nine million Niki posters, the better.
: You hear that, Niki?! Just because you’re hot and talented doesn’t mean I have to like you! Get bent!
: Oh, good. She has a rival now. Cute.
: Wow. I had no idea Miss Imai hated pop music this much.
: I'm glad she does. It will make it easier to convert her into one of my people.
: Now, come. Both of you.
: You haven’t seen the last of me, Niki! I’ll be back!
: Come on, Miss Imai. If you yell at the billboards any longer, people will think you’re crazy. Then no one will want to like you as hard as you apparently want to be liked.
: What was your name again? Karin?
: Yes! Hello!
: Grab her.
: What?
: Grab her. You’re tall and...powerful looking. And I am not about to be delayed by a woman too busy yelling at signs to remember we are here on a mission.
: I’m coming, damn it! I just needed to get my midday fury out of the way first.
: Wow...everything here is so...scary...
: It looks like a normal gothic lolita place to me.
: Yes, isn’t it wonderful?
: Now, I’m all for trying on a bunch of random shit and looking horrible in like 99%% of it, but I’m not sure if I like the idea of people thinking my Halloween costume is just “Black Wakana.”
: Why not? It’s better than “Hat Imani.”
: I like Hat Imani! It’s like normal Imani, just-
: With a hat. We know. Now, go run along and look at all of the dresses.
: Okay!
: And whatever you do, don’t go into the back room. That is for adults only.
: Got it! I like rules!
: Wakana, what kind of place did you take me to that has an “adults only” back room? I thought we were costume shopping.
: We are. It just also happens to be in the same place where I shop for chains and lingerie for Osako’s secret boudoir photo shoots.
: And which one of you is the photographer?
: Yes.
: God damn I need to get laid.
: Well, that’s on you for not taking your new rival up on her offer. You had your chance and squandered it.
: Yeah, I know. The six hours of listening to the two of them go at it is etched so deep into my memory at this point that I can pretty much replay the whole night in my head.
: Lucky.
: Wakana, is it weird to ask somebody to have friend-sex with you?
: Well, you’ve certainly chosen a strange time to start hitting on me.
: Not you. Senpai.
: You asked Arakawa to have sex with you?
: I’m not proud of it, okay? I just wanted to...test how much he’s actually into this idol friend of his.
: But...you would have followed through with it if he’d agreed, yes?
: Oh God yeah. I ain’t no baby-back bitch.
: Then...I take it you’ve already revealed your body to him?
: I...have not.

: Were you hoping he’d just...keep his eyes closed the entire time, then? Or are you so desperate for sex at this point that you’re willing to just overlook your self-image issues if it means relieving your tension?
: The former. And if he did not agree, I would have blindfolded him. I have several bandanas I have been saving for such an occasion.
: You’re really deep into this, aren’t you?
: Yeah, but it’s not like I want to be. I love what he and I have right now. You know that. I just...fucking...
: Ughhhhhhhhhhh! Why did I ask him that?! I made everything wooooooorse!
: I’m sure Arakawa didn’t mind...If anything, I imagine he took it as a compliment.
: Just...keep in mind that you aren’t the problem. He did say he likes you, didn’t he?
: Yeah...just not hard enough.
: The timing is just wrong, Imani. That happens sometimes. It’s not as if your life is over.
: Ughhhhhhhh but it feels like it iiiiiiiiiis.
: Moaning and groaning will get you nowhere. But do you know what will?
: Putting on a dress that’s way too big for me and then having you repeatedly tell me that I’d make a good goth when we all know I wouldn’t?
: Exactly.
: Hah...
: Black Wakana here I come...
: You know what? It’s probably good that Senpai turned down the friend-sex.
: Christ, are we still on this? I thought we were done.
: Think about it, though. Like, he’s boning an idol. And he’s not just boning her, he’s boning her a lot. I don’t have that kind of stamina. No way I’d be able to go that long.
: So, all things considered, if he did screw me, he’d probably just think, “Ehh. I’ve had better. Also, what’s with the blindfold?” and then it would just end.
: At least this way, we get to stay friends. And I can just keep hoping they break up or something and I can get him on the rebound when his standards are lower.
: Are you done? Can we move on now?
: Well, excuse me, princess. I didn’t realize there was a limit on how long I was allowed to talk about my feelings for.
: There’s no strict limit. But a time must come when you think to yourself, “You know what? I’ve been speaking for 75%% of the day and it is possible my friend might have something to say as well.”
: Well, do you?
: Do you not wear underwear with that outfit?
: That’s what you want to talk about? When I do and don’t wear underwear?
: It wasn’t originally. But I can’t help but bring it up now that you’re exposing your genitals to me.
: Well, ignoring my genitals, what was it you had to say?
: I can’t remember.
: That feeling when I’m closer to friend-sex with you than I am with Senpai.
: Wait, I remember now. And it should still pique your interest to some extent as Arakawa is still a part of it.
: If it has anything to do with him having sex with anyone other than me, I don’t want to hear it. I know too much already.
: Rest assured, it does not. In fact, it has more to do with his niece than it does with him.
: Ami? Why do you want to talk about Ami?
: You’re aware that she won my poetry contest, correct?
: I am. I’m shocked as well given how she fares in every subject other than creative writing, but still. I’m aware.
: And are you familiar with a poet who goes by the name “The Girl Who Cannot Breathe?”
: That, I am not. Poetry isn’t really one of my areas of expertise the way it is for you. But why do you ask? Do you think Ami may have been plagiarizing or something?
: It’s hard to say. The situation is...complicated.
: Complicated?
: Before I say any more, I need you to promise that you won’t repeat any of this to Arakawa. He’s rather...touchy when it comes to this subject.
: Senpai is touchy with something? But his whole thing is never being able to show any emotion about anything.
: Yes, well...I seem to have found the one area where that is not the case.
: Then, yeah. I won’t say anything to him. What’s up?
: Well, Ami’s work is remarkably similar to that of The Girl Who Cannot Breathe. So much so that I did initially worry that plagiarism could be at play.
: But now you think it’s not?
: Miss Imai? Miss Watabe? Can I come in?
: Yeah, you’re good.
: Thanks. And sorry to be a Debbie Downer, but I don’t think I’m going to find anything here. It seems like everything is mostly tailored to more...petite girls.
: I haven’t even tried anything on yet. But go on, Wakana. Finish what you wanted to say.
: Thank you. What I was in the process of saying is that I haven’t exactly ruled out plagiarism just yet, but I’m beginning to believe that this poet might actually be her mother.
: And that’s...an issue?
: It wouldn’t be an issue if it was just any poet. But the one in question had a remarkably grim view of the world that I fear may be...tainting one of your students. In an unhealthy way.
: Unhealthy how? Because if this is actually as dangerous as you’re making it sound, I should probably talk to her.
: I’m glad you’re of the same mindset as me while Arakawa couldn’t be more opposed if he tried.
: But what I mean by “unhealthy” is that The Girl Who Cannot Breathe makes Poe’s tastes seem tame by comparison.
: Oh damn. That guy was into some weird shit too.
: He was. But his tastes were not toxic, whereas the poet in question wanted people to feel the way she felt and empathize with these...disgusting, horrific ideals that just...
: They’re things that are okay to admire from afar and through a critical lens where we can sit back and cherry pick where the flaws in her manner of thinking were.
: But if these thoughts, ideals, and mannerisms are being replicated, which I believe seems to be the case, there’s cause for concern in the spread of this parasitic mindset as a whole.
: And I think we need to get to her before it becomes too much to bear.
: Got it. I’ll read some of her stuff when I get home tonight to get a better idea of what you’re talking about. Then, we can figure out where to go from there.
: You’re absolutely positive this is serious though, right? Because anything involving her parents isn't something we should bring up unless we absolutely have to.
: I think it could be. But that’s all we should need in order to intervene if Arakawa would rather let his niece just fall into a bottomless pit of debauchery without actually trying to stop it.
: Wait, have you guys been talking about Ami’s mom this whole time?
: Why? You don’t know something, do you?
: I don’t, but my dad might. He went to school with her.
: What?
: Is Ami okay? All that stuff about unhealthy ideals and...parasitic mindsets and stuff doesn’t really sound like-
: Karin, how sure are you about this? How do you know?
: I was showing my family pictures from the beach trip and my dad said Ami looked almost identical to a girl that used to be in his class.
: They didn’t have the same last name, so there was no way of being 100%% sure. But he seemed pretty adamant that she might be her daughter.
: I was planning on just leaving it at that since Ami’s really sensitive about stuff involving her parents, but if you really think she’s in trouble, I can try to-
: Don’t worry about Ami for now. Let’s leave her out of this until we have a little more to go off of.
: Karin, can you provide me with your father’s phone number? I’d like to speak with him about this if that’s okay.
: Yeah...if that will help, sure. I’ll do anything I can.
: That’s all you need to worry about for now, Karin. Wakana and I will take it from here.
: Imani is correct. But please, his number.
: Oh, right. It’s-
